cells.tense: Right now you are letting people watch you begin, and it is holding.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've rehearsed to death and give the rougher, truer version out loud to someone today.
cells.core:
You've got something going and you're not hiding it. People lean in because the eagerness is real and the direction is still forming — you don't need to know where it lands to mean it. That's what makes it land now: the fire is aimed at what's in front of you, not at a picture of later. What keeping it that bright costs is the flatness that comes after — so you add and take away as the day asks, some bold, some quiet, and you listen for the blend. The confidence that lands hardest is the one that's been tuned, not the one that's just loud.

Nothing asks you to dim it. Shine because something got built, not to keep the room warm — feed that one today.

cells.tense: You are already reading a chapter that hasn't been written while today's page sits open.
cells.ask: Take the smallest piece of what's in front of you and finish that one entirely before planning the next.
cells.core:
You've outrun your own work. The enthusiasm is still doing what enthusiasm does — lighting fires, pulling people along — but it's aimed at a version of things that doesn't exist yet, and the you that's here now keeps getting dragged toward it. You plan the launch before the thing is started. The feeling is real and it's yours; it's just not information yet. What you can do is small: act a little, ask one question, and let what's true settle before the next idea shoves it aside. The one who delivers what's actually here — the half-done, messy part — is the one who finds out what the fire is for.

One unfinished thing, all the way done, before the next spark gets its turn.

cells.tense: The fire went quiet a while back and you are still standing near it, not saying so.
cells.ask: Tell one person one small true thing about what you want next, without needing them to do anything about it.
cells.core:
The spark isn't gone, it's parked. Somewhere you learned that reaching out loud costs something you couldn't pay that time, so you got careful — and the carefulness reads well from the outside. It isn't coldness. It's a hand pulled back mid-air. The thing you stopped doing — starting, asking, letting people see you mid-reach — hasn't stopped being yours. You don't have to relight the whole blaze. You need one small tending: something material, something near, something you can hold in your hands. That's what gets the current moving again into the confidence you already earned.

Tend one small thing you can touch, and let it be enough.

cells.tense: You are carrying what you made like something that fell into your hands by luck.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, 'I made that,' about something solid you finished and have been handing the credit for to circumstance.
cells.core:
You made this. The confidence, the fire, the thing people lean into — that's yours, and you've been talking about it as if it happened to you. Someone gave you the idea that a real one doesn't keep score, and now what you built sits in another book. You don't need to argue with anyone about it. Just notice it — what got finished, what got carried, where your hand actually was on it — and stop filing your own work under luck, timing, or the room. That's the quieter strength: the one that doesn't need noise, only to stand where it is.

One thing you finished. Your name on it. Say it once, and don't take it back.
